query: Current official France or European guideline for ophthalmic and orbital tumours radiotherapy, including Institut Curie, SFRO, ESMO, EURACAN, SIOPE or ESTRO, verify publication date and canonical URL
response:
## Bottom line

There is **no single current pan-European guideline covering radiotherapy for every ophthalmic and orbital tumour**. The most authoritative documents are disease-specific:

1. **French broad radiotherapy reference:** the **2022 SFRO RecoRad chapter on malignant tumours of the eye and ocular adnexa**.
2. **European uveal-melanoma standard:** the **2023 ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for uveal melanoma**.
3. Orbital lymphoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, lacrimal-gland malignancy and orbital sarcoma are generally covered by their respective lymphoma, paediatric sarcoma, head-and-neck or soft-tissue-sarcoma pathways rather than one ophthalmic-radiotherapy guideline.

## Authoritative sources

| Scope | Document and authority | Publication status/date | Canonical or best authoritative URL | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Eye and ocular-adnexal malignancies; radiotherapy techniques and indications | **“Radiotherapy of malignant tumours of the eye and adnexa”**, part of the Société française de radiothérapie oncologique (**SFRO**) RecoRad recommendations | Published in *Cancer/Radiothérapie*, **volume 26, 2022**, in the SFRO recommendations issue | [Cancer/Radiothérapie, volume 26 issue index – ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/cancer-radiotherapie/vol/26/issue/1) | **Primary French professional guideline.** This is the most directly relevant French radiotherapy reference located. The journal issue is authoritative, but I could not safely verify an article-level DOI/PII from the retrieved material and therefore do not provide one. |
| Uveal melanoma: diagnosis, local treatment—including plaque brachytherapy, proton/charged-particle treatment and stereotactic approaches—and follow-up | **“Uveal melanoma: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up”** | *Annals of Oncology* **34(12), December 2023, pp. 1203–1218**; DOI **10.1016/j.annonc.2023.08.011** | [DOI landing page](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2023.08.011) | **Primary European multidisciplinary guideline.** This is the clearest current European guideline for adult uveal melanoma and should normally be used alongside national radiotherapy technique guidance. |
| UK uveal melanoma, including orbital adjuvant and palliative RT | **“Uveal Melanoma UK national guidelines: 2023 update”** | Published online in the *European Journal of Cancer* in **2025**; the document identifies itself as the 2023 update | [Journal full text](https://www.ejcancer.com/article/S0959-8049(25)00469-1/fulltext) | **Primary national guideline, but UK—not French or pan-European.** Useful as a recent comparator, particularly where the ESMO document is less technically detailed. |

## Findings for the named organisations

### Institut Curie

Institut Curie is a major French reference centre for ocular oncology and proton treatment, but its publicly accessible disease and treatment pages should be treated as **institutional patient-care information**, not automatically as a formally developed national clinical-practice guideline. For prescriptive French radiotherapy guidance, the **SFRO RecoRad document** is the stronger authority; for uveal melanoma, it should be paired with the **2023 ESMO guideline**.

I did not identify, from the retrieved evidence, a separately published current Institut Curie document that clearly declares a guideline methodology, consensus process, publication date and version control comparable with SFRO or ESMO. Accordingly, an Institut Curie webpage should not be cited as “the French guideline” unless a specific dated protocol or référentiel is supplied.

### SFRO

The **2022 eye-and-adnexa chapter in the SFRO RecoRad series** is the principal broad French radiotherapy source identified. It is a professional-society recommendation published in the society’s guideline issue of *Cancer/Radiothérapie*, rather than merely a centre-specific review. The exact article-level canonical URL could not be verified from the retrieved records, so the journal issue URL above is supplied without inventing a DOI.

### ESMO

The **2023 ESMO uveal-melanoma guideline** is the strongest current European disease-specific document identified. Its date and DOI are bibliographically identifiable: *Annals of Oncology*, December 2023, DOI [10.1016/j.annonc.2023.08.011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2023.08.011).

### EURACAN

EURACAN covers rare adult solid cancers, including rare ocular cancers through its rare-cancer network activity, but I did not verify a separate, current **EURACAN-branded ophthalmic/orbital radiotherapy guideline** from the retrieved material. Do not describe the ESMO uveal-melanoma guideline as “ESMO–EURACAN” unless the title or official record explicitly carries that joint designation.

### ESTRO

I did not verify a current standalone **ESTRO clinical guideline encompassing ophthalmic and orbital tumours as a group**. ESTRO publications may address individual techniques—particularly brachytherapy, particle therapy, stereotactic radiotherapy or target delineation—but those should not be represented as a comprehensive ocular-oncology guideline without an exact title and society endorsement.

### SIOPE

For children, particularly **orbital rhabdomyosarcoma and retinoblastoma**, management is protocol- and disease-group-specific. I did not verify a current public SIOPE document devoted specifically to “ophthalmic and orbital tumour radiotherapy.” SIOPE/European paediatric soft-tissue-sarcoma protocols may govern orbital rhabdomyosarcoma, but they are not interchangeable with the adult SFRO or ESMO documents and may not be publicly available in their current protocol form.

## Practical citation hierarchy

For a French or European radiotherapy protocol, the defensible hierarchy is:

1. **Uveal melanoma:** cite the **2023 ESMO guideline** as the European disease-management standard, then use the **2022 SFRO RecoRad eye/adnexa chapter** for French radiotherapy practice.
2. **Other adult ocular or adnexal tumours:** start with the **2022 SFRO chapter**, supplemented by the relevant disease guideline—for example lymphoma, sarcoma, skin cancer or head-and-neck guidance.
3. **Paediatric orbital tumours:** use the current tumour-group protocol, particularly for rhabdomyosarcoma or retinoblastoma; do not extrapolate adult uveal-melanoma recommendations.
4. **Institut Curie material:** use as centre-specific implementation or patient information unless the document is explicitly labelled, dated and methodologically documented as a guideline.

The two documents that can presently be identified most confidently as the core authorities are therefore the **SFRO 2022 recommendation** and the **ESMO 2023 uveal-melanoma guideline**.
